scope: tmux 3.8 filtered event waits and receipt-backed pane state monitors

claims_checked: wait-for -E waits for events, -F filters event payloads, -v prints payload, and -l lists waiters
set-hook -B monitors a format once per second and fires a user event when the value changes
the first monitor sample records a baseline without firing an event
tmux 3.8 introduced event-based hooks, wait-for -E, and set-hook -B monitors
wait-for -E attaches a named event sink and removes it after a matching event
monitor values are sampled once per second and the first value initializes the baseline

binary.server_scope: Each integration test used a unique temporary directory and explicit private -S socket with /dev/null configuration.

targeting.wait_event: One exact pane ID per allowlisted event; caller-provided format strings are rejected.
targeting.wait_state: One registry-bound pane whose task, endpoint, server, pane PID, window, and process identity match; closed records are rejected.
targeting.state_policy: Policy allow_monitor is required. Task and registry state plus policy are rechecked under the operation lock before receipt creation and before monitor installation.
targeting.hooks: A receipt-backed unique user event and one pane-local fixed-format monitor are installed without a hook command. The event waiter is confirmed in wait-for -E -l before installation. Cleanup removes a monitor only after exact definition and server identity checks.

focused_tests.result: 13 passed; 9 tmux 3.8 integration tests skipped because GOALS_TMUX38_BINARY was not set.
checks: bounded streaming rejects output above 64 KiB
empty, duplicate, and mismatched event payloads are rejected
tmux 3.6a and missing-server capability probes fail closed
a live PID with an unmatched start string remains unknown; only ProcessLookupError proves absence
exact pane-exited wait ignores an earlier sibling-pane exit
pane-died event is observed with remain-on-exit
timeout disconnect leaves no event waiter
pane_title change is observed and the exact monitor is removed
pane_dead change on a retained pane is observed and cleaned up after the pane PID disappears
state timeout removes its monitor and settles its receipt
monitor policy denial writes no receipt, and a task entering finalizing before install receives no monitor
reconcile removes an exact orphan monitor and verifies absence
reconcile preserves a mismatched hook and does not contact a replacement server while the old PID is alive
live_tests.cleanup: All tests used per-test private sockets and called kill-server only against those exact sockets. A post-run process scan found no tmux process using the isolated 3.8 binary.

cli_acceptance.summary: The packaged CLI observed pane_title change and timeout with monitor cleanup, reported 3.6a event features unavailable, and settled the managed task after close.

conservative_reconciliation.server_replaced: A different server identity is not enough to settle a receipt. The old server PID must be proven absent first; a live PID with a mismatching start string remains unknown to cover PID reuse and timezone/locale differences.
conservative_reconciliation.hook_conflict: If an event name exists with a different monitor definition, reconciliation leaves it untouched and keeps the receipt pending.

limitations: Only the seven listed pane events are exposed; no window- or session-event allowlist is claimed.
tmux monitor sampling is once per second. Very brief state changes between samples may not be observed.
pane-command-started, pane-command-finished, and pane-shell-prompt events do not prove the target shell emitted OSC 133 markers in every environment.
If a server PID still exists but its saved OS start string cannot be matched, the old monitor receipt remains unsettled rather than assuming the server exited.
